_readme: Links, never weights. No file above 2 GB is committed. fetch_artifact.py tries drive_id first (gdown --id, the owner's own 5 TB drive), then hf_url, then each entry in hf_urls. On success it writes .services/assets.lock.json with the real byte count and sha256, and every later run verifies against that instead of trusting a manifest someone typed once. Set sha256 to null to accept whatever the first successful download produces, then copy the value from the lock into this file to pin it.

sd-turbo.why: A single-file SD1.5-family checkpoint that ComfyUI loads as-is. Small enough to download in a CI job, light enough to render 512x512 in well under a minute on four CPU cores. Rename it to whatever COMFY_CKPT says.

sd-fast.why: Optional faster path: an LCM/turbo checkpoint, if one is uploaded to Drive. The built-in graph uses 4 steps when this is present.
